title: Three Index Managers Hold 22% of a Typical S&P 500 Company
hook: Index funds grew into concentrated ownership and voting power.
closing: Your fund owns the shares, but its manager usually casts the corporate votes.
question: Who votes the shares in your fund?

segments.say: Passive index funds reached 52 percent of US stock-market assets. Routine investing created enormous collective ownership.
BlackRock, Vanguard, and State Street together hold 22 percent of a typical large company. Ownership concentrates behind familiar fund names.
Vanguard alone casts 9 percent of votes at large-company meetings. Fund ownership becomes corporate voting power.
